newsitem.title: SPAIN: Italy's Berlusconi in Spain legal wrangle.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi in Spain legal wrangle.

text.p: Confusion surrounded reports on Thursday that Spain's High Court had charged Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi for tax and investment violations related to his media group Fininvest.
Leading Spanish newspaper El Pais reported that the High Court had charged Berlusconi and 37 others with tax and investment violations.
Berlusconi and media group Fininvest which holds a stake in Spanish television channel Telecinco, denied they had committed any crimes relating to their investments in Spain.

"(Fininvest) reiterates once more that it has never owned stakes that exceeded the limit established by existing laws and is certain to be able to show the absolute correctness of its operations, incuding the fiscal ones," the media group said in a statement issued in Rome.

Officials at the High Court declined to comment on the report, and anti-corruption prosecutors investigating the case would only confirm that they had asked that 38 people including Berlusconi be charged.
The prosecutors' office said they were investigating Fininvest investments in television channel Telecinco.
El Pais reported that Judge Baltasar Garzon, at the request of prosecutors, filed charges against Berlusconi and others for violating a variety of tax and corporate laws.

Spanish anti-corruption prosecutors said in a statement that Fininvest had violated limits set out in Spain's Private Television law which says that a single shareholder can only hold 25 percent in a television station.

"Fininvest illegally exceeded this limit by possessing more than 80 percent of Telecinco's capital and used companies, people and resident bank accounts in third countries to fake fictitious ownership," it said.

But in comments made to journalists and reported by Italian agency Ansa, Berlusconi said there were no irregularities in the ownership of stakes in Telecinco and that company officals "were acting for the benefit of the television channel and the interests of the group".
Prosecutors said those in charge at Fininvest had also evaded taxes of nearly two billion pesetas ($13 million).
"As a result, we have asked that 38 people including Silvio Berlusconi be charged," the prosecutors said.
The High Court ordered a search of Telecinco's offices on Wednesday. The television station said that transfers of shares had always passed through the appropriate authorities.
"Telecinco is convinced that all its activities have conformed more strictly than the prevailing law," the station said in statement.

Berlusconi, who governed Italy for seven turbulent months in 1994, is already standing trial in Italy for alleged false accounting related to Fininvest. In separate cases he faces charges of bribing tax inspectors in return for lenient audits of his companies and for illegally channelling funds to politicians.
